about.title: Sand City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Sand City is a small coastal community in Monterey County, but its stretch of SR-1, SR-1 Southbound, and California Avenue still carry steady traffic between Monterey and Seaside. Public crash records for the most recent final year show zero reported injury collisions in the city, which is a good sign, but it doesn't mean every trip is free of risk, and collisions can still happen without always making it into a finalized report the same year they occur. Reported crashes here tend to cluster on Wednesday mornings between 8 and 10 a.m., which lines up with commuter and delivery traffic squeezing through this tight coastal corridor. If you were injured in a car accident anywhere in Sand City, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who can look at what happened, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid mistakes that could hurt your claim later. There's no cost to get connected and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Starts Now
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like a city or Caltrans, is involved. Given how many California roadways run through Sand City, it's worth having someone check this early.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly at fault, though your share of fault can reduce the amount. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you before you've even had a chance to respond.

items.title: Don't Give the Other Insurer a Recorded Statement Yet
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly, before you know the full extent of your injuries. California law doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so it's worth talking to an independent attorney first so an early statement doesn't limit what you're able to pursue later.

items.question: I was in a crash on SR-1 near Sand City and the other insurer already called me. Should I talk to them?
items.answer: It's usually best to hold off on giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an independent attorney, since early statements can be used to minimize your claim later. You're not required to provide one right away. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can advise you on what to say, if anything, before you respond.

items.question: The public records show no injury crashes in Sand City last year. Does that mean my accident wasn't serious?
items.answer: Not at all. That number reflects finalized statewide reporting for the city as a whole, and it doesn't diminish or dictate the outcome of your specific accident. Your injuries and their impact on your life are what matter for a claim, not how your crash compares to citywide totals.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Sand City?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit, but if a government entity or public road maintenance issue was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months. Given the mix of state highway and local roads running through Sand City, it's worth having an attorney confirm which deadline applies to your situation as soon as possible.
